target_customer: Nigerian households with prepaid meters, and electricity utilities that pay BuyPower a share of each purchase
problem: Paying for prepaid electricity in Nigeria meant queues and outdated utility payment systems.
business_model: Percentage of each power purchase plus a per transaction fee charged to utilities

founders.name: Ojima Benjamin Ufaruna
prior_employers: A technology development services company in Abuja (unnamed)
founders.background_notes: TechCrunch (2017-03) says the founders met at a technology services company in Abuja.

founders.name: Asehinde Oladipo
prior_employers: A technology development services company in Abuja (unnamed)
founders.background_notes: Listed as Chief Operations Officer on the YC page.

technical_complexity.rationale: Required integrating with utility back ends and upgrading their payment systems, per TechCrunch (2017-03).

defensibility.rationale: Utilities integrated with BuyPower's software and the founders covered rollout costs, which creates integration lock in.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No acquisition found. Later profiles name Paga, Quickteller, Flutterwave and OPay as alternative channels.

market_need_then: TechCrunch (2017-03) reported about 40 percent of the paid electricity market in Abuja and roughly 1M USD monthly revenue within a year of the April 2016 launch.

branding.domain_note: Uses buypower.ng, a country domain rather than .com.

identity.voice_and_tone: Helpful consumer utility guides on its blog

branding.community_and_virality: Third party guides on Legit.ng and Dignited explain how to use buypower.ng.

brand_strength.rationale: Descriptive name that says what it does; guides by outlets show recognition among Nigerian users but no brand specific press was found.

outcome_analysis: BuyPower gained about 40 percent of Abuja prepaid electricity payments within a year by integrating directly with utilities, and the company is still operating with a listed team of 115. Reported revenue and funding come from profiles and are unverified, but nothing suggests failure.
notes: Funding unverified: Seedtable lists a 120K seed in March 2017 from Y Combinator with Musha Ventures and Aston Motes, and Liners lists 130K across two rounds. These look like YC standard deal data from aggregators, so no round is recorded. Profiles claim about 20.6M revenue in December 2024; unverified. The TechCrunch article names no competitors, so the list is empty; Quickteller and Paga guides found were undated. A sponsored article describes an Aella partnership that is not funding. Founder education not found.
